title: Regular schemes locally of finite type over a perfect field are smooth
statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field, meaning that every algebraic field extension of $k$ is separable. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $X$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. No separatedness, integrality, nonemptiness or dimension assumption is imposed.

theorem smooth_of_isRegular {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsRegular X] : Smooth f
lean.note: Existing source declaration in WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Regular.lean, verified against the current server source. The signature is verbatim: perfect field k, scheme X, f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k), LocallyOfFiniteType f and IsRegular X, concluding Smooth f. IsRegular alone means only regular local stalks, not the full regular-scheme notion of def-weil-regular-scheme. Here Spec k is locally Noetherian and LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f supplies IsLocallyNoetherian X. Consequently Stacks 02IT identifies IsRegular X with the dependency node's affine-neighbourhood regularity under the other hypotheses of this theorem; no local-Noetherian hypothesis is dropped or added. The shared universe is imposed by the scheme morphism to Spec k. The dependency record is retained unchanged. A fresh scompile probe checks the declaration and its axioms.
